Trade Analyzer

See what any trade does to both teams' lineups and playoff, title and last-place odds.

How it works & FAQ›

What is this?

A trade tool built on our ESPN league, so the teams, rosters, records and schedule are the real ones. It has three modes: Analyzer grades a trade you build, Finder searches every roster for deals that help you (or for the best return on a player you want to move), and Needs shows where each team is strong or thin.

How does it decide whether a trade is good?

It works out each team's best starting lineup for every remaining week, before and after the trade, then plays out the rest of the season about 4,000 times using the real schedule, standings and playoff format, including the consolation ladder that decides last place. That gives each team's playoff, title and last-place odds. The verdict weighs title odds most, then playoff odds, and counts last-place odds against you, so for a team with no real playoff shot, staying out of last still counts as a win. The report shows the effect on both teams.

Where does the data come from?

Rosters, records, schedule and settings come from our ESPN league. Player values are rest-of-season points per game: ESPN's projection blended with FantasyPros', plus a light adjustment for how each player has actually scored this season. The green and red FP badges flag players FantasyPros rates notably higher or lower than ESPN.

What do the numbers mean?

Pts/g is projected points per game for the rest of the season, and the small S marks a player who starts next week. In the report, Title odds, Playoff odds, Last place and Lineup pts/week show before and after for both teams. The tabs below break down the reasoning, and Counter-offers suggests a one-player change that would make a lopsided deal work for both sides.

How current is it?

It's a snapshot, not a live feed. The header shows the week and the date of the last refresh, and it's updated through the season. The Finder also shows how long is left before the trade deadline.

How much should I trust it?

Treat it as a decision aid, not a crystal ball. Projections are estimates and the odds come from simulations, so the season will play out differently. It's best for comparing options and spotting deals that are clearly good, bad or lopsided, not for exact percentages.
